## Answer Key & Explanations

**Q1. (d)** — Vande Mataram was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay (c. 1875), featured in his novel Anandamath, and was adopted as the National Song by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950; 2026 marks its 150th year.

**Q2. (d)** — The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay (Gowalia Tank) session of the AICC, where Gandhi gave the mantra 'Do or Die' and the resolution demanded an immediate end to British rule.

**Q3. (a)** — The first INC session was held in December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, presided over by Womesh Chandra (W. C.) Bonnerjee, with A. O. Hume as a key organiser.

**Q4. (a)** — Lord Curzon announced the Partition of Bengal, which came into effect on 16 October 1905, sparking the Swadeshi and Boycott movements. It was annulled in 1911 under Lord Hardinge.

**Q5. (c)** — The Champaran Satyagraha (1917), against the oppressive tinkathia indigo system in Bihar, was Gandhi's first satyagraha on Indian soil. Kheda (1918) and the Ahmedabad mill strike (1918) followed.

**Q6. (d)** — On 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi), General Dyer ordered firing on a peaceful crowd gathered at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, protesting the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of leaders like Saifuddin Kitchlew and Satyapal.

**Q7. (a)** — After a mob at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, UP) set fire to a police station killing policemen on 5 February 1922, Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement, citing the turn to violence.

**Q8. (a)** — The Indian Statutory (Simon) Commission had no Indian member, provoking the 'Simon Go Back' protests. Lala Lajpat Rai was injured in a lathi charge during a demonstration at Lahore and later died.

**Q9. (b)** — At the Lahore session (December 1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Congress adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution, and 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day.

**Q10. (a)** — Gandhi's Salt March (12 March-6 April 1930) went about 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi, where he broke the salt law. Dharasana was the site of a later salt raid.

**Q11. (d)** — The Poona Pact (September 1932) between Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar replaced the separate electorates for the Depressed Classes (proposed under the Communal Award) with reserved seats within the general electorate.

**Q12. (d)** — Subhas Chandra Bose assumed INA leadership in 1943 at Singapore, proclaimed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind, and the INA included the Rani of Jhansi Regiment, an all-women combat unit led by Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal.

**Q13. (d)** — The Cabinet Mission (1946) rejected the demand for a sovereign Pakistan, proposed a three-tier federal structure with grouping of provinces, an interim government, and a Constituent Assembly to frame the Constitution.

**Q14. (b)** — The sepoys revolted at Meerut on 10 May 1857 and marched to Delhi, proclaiming Bahadur Shah Zafar as emperor. Mangal Pandey's earlier act was at Barrackpore (29 March 1857).

**Q15. (c)** — The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; Lord William Bentinck became the first to hold this title. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (Regulating Act, 1773).

**Q16. (b)** — The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly over trade with India (except the tea trade and trade with China). The 1833 Act ended commercial functions; the 1853 Act introduced open competition for the civil services.

**Q17. (b)** — Lord William Bentinck, supported by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, abolished Sati through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829. The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act came later, in 1856.

**Q18. (b)** — Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, a teacher at Hindu College, Calcutta, inspired the Young Bengal Movement, whose members ('Derozians') attacked orthodox customs and championed free thought and reason.

**Q19. (b)** — The Kakori train action (August 1925) was carried out by the Hindustan Republican Association. Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were executed for their role.

**Q20. (b)** — Bhagat Singh and B. K. Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929 on behalf of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), aiming 'to make the deaf hear', and courted arrest.

**Q21. (a)** — Bal Gangadhar Tilak launched his Home Rule League at Poona (April 1916) and Annie Besant launched hers at Madras (September 1916), demanding self-government for India within the Empire.

**Q22. (a)** — The Lucknow Pact (1916) marked joint Congress-Muslim League action on constitutional reform; the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims. The same session also saw reunion of Moderates and Extremists.

**Q23. (b)** — Birsa Munda led the Munda rebellion or 'Ulgulan' (1899-1900) in the Chhotanagpur region. His birth anniversary (15 November) is now observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

**Q24. (a)** — Lord Lytton's government passed the Vernacular Press Act (1878) to restrict Indian-language newspapers; it was repealed in 1882 by his successor Lord Ripon.

**Q25. (c)** — Charles Wood's Despatch of 1854, the 'Magna Carta of English education in India', recommended a graded system of education, English and vernacular instruction, teacher training and grants-in-aid, and led to setting up universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras (1857).
